messages:
Alex Gomez: hey! first day setup question — Kandji finished enrollment but FileVault didn't prompt and my login shows a local account only. I also don't see my Okta device record. should i force a re-enroll or is there a step I missed?

Mia (IT): welcome Alex :tada: can you confirm macOS version and whether you used the company USB-C dock during first boot? sometimes docks mess with disk encryption prompts.

Alex Gomez: macOS 14.4, plugged into docking station at my desk (supply provided). enrollment said completed. Kandji-bot message popped but no FileVault dialog.

Kandji-bot: Enrollment complete for "Alex Gomez - MacBookAir15" at 2026-08-02T09:12:05Z. Applied profile: "New Hire 14".

Jordan (Device Admin): odd. Kandji should force FileVault enablement and trigger the recovery key escrow. Two guesses: 1) the preexisting local account meant FileVault was already enabled earlier but not escrowed, or 2) a network hiccup prevented sending the recovery key to Okta/KMS during first-run. Can you run sudo fdesetup status and paste output? Also send the serial number (we'll look up device record).

Alex Gomez: output: "FileVault is Off". Serial: C02AX1Y9L4JF.

Mia (IT): thanks. i see the device in our MDM but Okta doesn't show a synced device. Jordan — can you check whether the escrow job failed?

Jordan (Device Admin): checking logs... looks like the escrow agent attempted to POST to okta-api.redwood.example but got "403 Forbidden" at 09:13:22. That generally means the service token wasn't present in the machine's secure store at the time of the call. Might be the dock delaying network reachability until after the agent ran. Workarounds: 1) Run the FileVault enablement flow manually (sudo fdesetup enable -user <username> and then vote the recovery key) and then run kandji's "SyncRecoveryKey" action. 2) Re-enroll with wifi-only or unplug dock for first-boot. Which do you prefer?

Alex Gomez: i'm fine running a command if you give it to me. don't want to re-enroll if avoidable.

Mia (IT): Jordan, can you paste the safe command and the exact kandji action name? i'll be on standby to approve any admin prompts.

Jordan (Device Admin): run these in Terminal (you'll be prompted for your password):

```
sudo fdesetup enable -user "alex.gomez"
# After you set a unlock password, run:
kandjictl runAction --device "C02AX1Y9L4JF" --action SyncRecoveryKey
```

If kandjictl isn't installed locally, i'll trigger the action from console after you enable. Note: if the system asks to create a recovery key, choose "Institutional recovery key" so it escrows back to Okta/KMS.

Alex Gomez: running now... prompted for password, then system asked: "Create a personal recovery key or institutional?" choosing institutional.

Rory: FYI we saw a couple dock-related enrollments yesterday where network was delayed and recovery key escrow failed. We'll add a one-liner to the new-hires doc: "If using dock: unplug until after enrollment completes or enable FV via wifi and run SyncRecoveryKey."

Okta-bot: Recovery escrow succeeded for device serial C02AX1Y9L4JF at 2026-08-02T09:18:40Z. Device now visible in Okta Devices.

Alex Gomez: ok looks like Okta shows my device now and login shows corporate account. FileVault status?

Mia (IT): Jordan — check fdesetup remotely or Alex run sudo fdesetup status again.

Alex Gomez: "FileVault is On." woo! thanks all.

Jordan (Device Admin): great. i'll update KB and queue an ops note for provisioning hardware (dock -> wifi-first). Alex — i'll also attach the incident in case networking wants to add a DHCP rule for faster link-up but this is low priority.

Alex Gomez: appreciate it. strolling to my desk now :grinning:"
